passages.text: A cold is a viral infection of the upper respiratory tract (also called an upper respiratory infection or URI). Colds usually last less than a week and are caused by different respiratory viruses.

The signs and symptoms of a cold usually peak within 2 to 3 days of infection and can include runny nose, nasal congestion, cough, sneezing, sore throat, headache, mild body aches, and fever (usually low grade in older children and adults).
SARS-CoV-2 (the virus that causes COVID-19), influenza virus (the virus that causes flu), and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) can also cause cold-like symptoms but do not cause colds.
